requirements.summary: A modern, highly animated landing page for a healthcare software platform. It features a sticky header with complex mega-menus, a split-pane hero section with sequential UI animations, a sticky-scroll features section, a scroll-driven problem/solution transition with SVG animations, and a grid of feature cards. The design relies heavily on a specific color palette (dark green, light green, light blue/gray) and elegant serif typography for headings.
requirements.template_goal: Create a reusable, component-driven template. Centralize design tokens in Tailwind configuration. Implement complex scroll-driven and sequential animations using a robust library (like Framer Motion or GSAP) to ensure smooth performance and maintainability. Ensure all copy, navigation links, and images are easily configurable via constants or props.
hard_constraints: The header must remain sticky at the top of the viewport during scroll.
The 'Resources' and 'What We Offer' navigation items must trigger full-width mega-menus on hover.
The hero section must be split into two distinct colored blocks with rounded corners.
The right side of the hero must contain an animated sequence of three UI cards (CRM, EHR, RCM).
The features section must use a sticky layout where the right content remains fixed while the left list scrolls.
The problem/solution section must use scroll-linked animations to transition text and animate SVG lines converging.

section_requirements.name: Header
section_requirements.purpose: Primary site navigation and call to action.
section_requirements.layout: Flex container, space-between. Logo left, nav links center, CTA right. Sticky top.
styling: Background white, slightly translucent with backdrop blur.
Button dark green background, white text, fully rounded.
behaviors: Hovering 'Resources' opens a mega-menu with Blog, Resources, Glossary.
Hovering 'What We Offer' opens a mega-menu with columns for CRM, EHR, RCM and their respective features.

section_requirements.name: Hero
section_requirements.purpose: Introduce the value proposition and show a glimpse of the product.
section_requirements.layout: Two-column grid or flex layout with a gap. Both columns have large rounded corners.
styling: Left column: Light green background, dark green text.
Large border radii (e.g., 24px) on both columns.
copy_items: Admit more patients, reduce staff burden, and get paid faster with an AI-native system built for behavioral healthcare.
assets: UI component SVGs or mockups for CRM, EHR, RCM cards
behaviors: On load, the three UI cards in the right column animate in sequentially (fade and slide up), connected by an animated line.

section_requirements.name: Logo Cloud
section_requirements.layout: Vertical flex: small heading above a horizontal flex row of logos, wrapping if necessary.
styling: Logos should be grayscale or muted, with consistent height.

section_requirements.name: Sticky Features
section_requirements.purpose: Highlight supported specialties while keeping the main value prop visible.
section_requirements.layout: Two-column layout. Left column scrolls, right column is sticky.
must_include: Sticky informational card with badge, text, and stats
styling: Left column: Large serif text. Active item is dark, inactive items are faded.
Right column: Light green background, rounded corners. Badge is small and pill-shaped.
copy_items: Ease is built from the ground up for behavioral health practices, with AI at the core.
behaviors: As the user scrolls, the right column sticks to the viewport.
The items in the left column change opacity based on their position in the viewport (scroll-spy effect).

section_requirements.name: Problem Solution Transition
section_requirements.purpose: Visually demonstrate the consolidation of fragmented systems.
section_requirements.layout: Single column, centered content. Large text area above an SVG animation area.
styling: Background transitions or is a solid light color.
copy_items: Fragmented CRM, EHR, and RCM systems are inefficient. They slow intake, burden staff, and hide revenue leakage.
Instead of bouncing between CRM, EHR, and RCM systems, Ease provides one AI-powered system for referrals, clinical notes, and billing.
behaviors: Scroll-linked animation: As the user scrolls through the section, the badge text changes from 'The problem' to 'The solution'.
The paragraph text crossfades to the new text.
An SVG graphic of multiple horizontal lines on the left animates to converge into a single line on the right.

section_requirements.name: Why Ease Cards
section_requirements.purpose: Detail specific benefits of the platform.
section_requirements.layout: Header area followed by a 3-column CSS grid of cards.
must_include: Three feature cards with icons, titles, and descriptions
styling: Cards have light green backgrounds, rounded corners.
copy_items: Consolidate tools, reduce spend, and gain unified reporting without painful integrations.
AI support helps admins, clinicians, supervisors, and billers complete important tasks in less time.
AI-driven billing engine and expert services run in the background so you collect more, faster.
behaviors: Cards fade in and slide up slightly as they enter the viewport.

layout_requirements: Use a max-width container (e.g., max-w-7xl) for main content to keep it centered on large screens.
Ensure generous padding between sections (e.g., py-24 or py-32).
Use CSS Grid for the 3-column feature cards to ensure equal heights and proper spacing.
Use Flexbox for the split hero section, allowing it to stack on smaller viewports.
styling_requirements: Apply the defined serif font to all major headings.
Use the specific light green (#D8EED9) and light blue (#B8D0D3) for large background areas.
Ensure all buttons have full border-radius (rounded-full).
Use subtle backdrop-blur on the sticky header.
copy_requirements: Ensure all text matches the provided copy exactly, including punctuation.
Group copy into a configuration object or separate file if the framework allows, to make future edits easy.
asset_requirements: Use SVG for logos and icons to ensure crisp rendering.
For the UI mockups in the hero, recreate them using HTML/CSS if possible, or use high-res SVGs. Do not use low-res PNGs.
behavior_requirements: The header must transition smoothly to a sticky state with a shadow/blur when scrolling past the top.
Mega-menus must open on hover with a slight fade-in and slide-down animation.
The scroll-spy in the features section must accurately track the active item based on scroll position.
animation_requirements: Hero right pane: Trigger on load. Sequence: CRM card fades/slides in, then EHR card, then RCM card. A connecting line should draw between them.

Problem/Solution: Trigger on scroll. Sequence: As the section enters the viewport, pin it. Scrub the animation based on scroll progress. Text crossfades. SVG paths animate their 'd' attribute or use stroke-dashoffset to show lines converging.
Why Ease cards: Trigger on scroll into view. Sequence: Staggered fade-in and slide-up (e.g., 100ms delay between each card).
structure_guidance: Break the page down into distinct components: Header, Hero, LogoCloud, StickyFeatures, ProblemSolution, FeatureCards.
Create a separate component for the MegaMenu to keep the Header component clean.
Encapsulate complex animation logic (like the scroll-linked SVG) within its own component to avoid cluttering the main page layout.
execution_plan: 1. Initialize project and configure Tailwind with the provided design tokens (colors, fonts, radii).
2. Build the Header component. Implement the basic layout, then add the hover logic and animations for the mega-menus.
3. Build the Hero section. Set up the split layout. Implement the left side content. For the right side, build the UI cards and implement the sequential entrance animation.
5. Build the Sticky Features section. Set up the CSS for the sticky right column. Implement JavaScript/React logic to track scroll position and update the opacity of the left list items.

6. Build the Problem/Solution section. This is the most complex. Set up the layout, then implement the scroll-linked animation using a library like Framer Motion (useScroll, useTransform) or GSAP ScrollTrigger. Animate the text swap and the SVG paths.
7. Build the Why Ease section. Set up the CSS grid and implement the scroll-triggered staggered entrance animation.
8. Perform a final review against the video reference, checking all animations, hover states, and responsive behaviors.
known_unknowns: The exact easing curves and durations for the animations are estimated; they may need fine-tuning to match the reference perfectly.
The exact behavior of the mega-menus on mobile is not shown in the desktop reference.
The specific SVG path data for the converging lines animation will need to be generated or approximated.

interaction_checkpoints.name: Header Mega-menu - Resources
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: A full-width dropdown panel appears smoothly, displaying links for Blog, Resources, and Glossary.

interaction_checkpoints.name: Header Mega-menu - What We Offer
interaction_checkpoints.trigger: Hover over 'What We Offer' link in header.
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: A full-width dropdown panel appears smoothly, displaying three columns (CRM, EHR, RCM) with lists of features under each.

interaction_checkpoints.name: Hero Animation
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: The three UI cards in the right pane of the hero section appear sequentially with a fade and slide-up motion.

interaction_checkpoints.name: Sticky Features Scroll
interaction_checkpoints.trigger: Scroll down to the features list.
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: The right panel ('Broad clinical support') sticks to the screen. As scrolling continues, the items in the left list highlight sequentially.

interaction_checkpoints.name: Problem/Solution Transition
interaction_checkpoints.expected_result: The text changes from 'The problem' to 'The solution', and the animated lines converge from multiple to one.

acceptance_criteria: The layout matches the split-pane and grid structures seen in the reference.
All colors, typography, and border radii match the defined design tokens.
The header is sticky and mega-menus function correctly on hover.
The hero section animations play smoothly on load.
The sticky features section correctly highlights the active item while keeping the right panel fixed.
The problem/solution scroll animation works smoothly, swapping text and animating the lines.
All copy is accurate and easily editable in the code structure.

validation.summary: The candidate establishes a good foundational layout and utilizes a strong configuration object for editability. However, there are critical failures in animation fidelity (specifically the Problem/Solution SVG curves), missing content in the rendered output (Hero RCM card and Why Ease cards), and structural mismatches in the mega-menus compared to the reference video.
strengths: Excellent use of a centralized JavaScript configuration object (`SITE_COPY`) for easy editing of copy and assets.
Color palette and typography choices closely match the provided design tokens.
The sticky header transition (background blur and shadow) works well.
The scroll-spy logic for the Sticky Features section correctly highlights active items.

issues.title: Incorrect Problem/Solution SVG Animation
issues.observed: The SVG animation uses straight `<line>` elements that simply move vertically on the Y-axis, creating a rigid, mechanical effect.
issues.expected: The animation must use smooth bezier curves that organically bend and converge into a single point, as seen in the reference video.
issues.fix_instructions: Replace the `<line>` elements in `#converge-svg` with `<path>` elements. Use GSAP to animate the `d` attribute, transitioning from straight horizontal paths to curved paths (using 'C' or 'S' bezier commands) that meet at the target coordinate.

issues.title: Missing Hero Card in Right Column
issues.observed: The third UI card (RCM) is cut off or missing from the rendered right column of the Hero section, and the EHR card is partially truncated.
issues.expected: All three UI cards (CRM, EHR, RCM) should be fully visible and stacked within the light blue container.
issues.fix_instructions: Ensure the right column container (`bg-secondary-light`) expands to fit its contents. Remove any implicit height constraints or adjust the padding/spacing so all three cards render fully within the box.

issues.title: Inaccurate Mega-Menu Layouts
issues.observed: The 'What We Offer' mega-menu is a simple grid. It lacks the complex two-pane layout seen in the video.
issues.expected: The 'What We Offer' dropdown should feature a distinct layout with a left-hand sidebar (often with a different background color) and a wider right-hand area containing the columns.
issues.fix_instructions: Redesign the `.mega-offer` HTML structure to include a flex or grid layout with a distinct left sidebar area and a right content area, matching the visual structure in the video.

issues.title: Invisible 'Why Ease' Cards
issues.observed: The three feature cards in the 'Why Ease' section do not appear in the rendered screenshot, likely due to scroll-trigger animation state issues.
issues.expected: The cards should be visible. If relying on scroll animations, they must trigger reliably or have a robust fallback.
issues.fix_instructions: Remove `opacity: 0` and `transform` from the base `.why-card` CSS. Instead, use `gsap.from()` in your ScrollTrigger setup to animate them from an invisible state. This ensures they default to visible if the JS doesn't execute perfectly during rendering.

issues.title: Hero Connecting Line Style
issues.observed: The connecting line behind the Hero cards is dashed.
issues.expected: The connecting line in the reference video is a solid line that appears to draw downwards.
issues.fix_instructions: Change `stroke-dasharray="4 4"` to a solid stroke and use `stroke-dashoffset` animation to draw the line in sequentially with the cards.

patch_instructions: In the `#converge-svg`, replace all `<line>` tags with `<path>` tags. Update the GSAP ScrollTrigger logic to animate the `d` attribute of these paths to create smooth bezier curves converging to the right side.
In the Hero section, check the flex properties and padding of the `.bg-secondary-light` container to ensure it grows tall enough to display all three `.hero-card` elements without cutting them off.

Update the CSS for `.why-card` to remove `opacity: 0` and `transform: translateY(40px)`. Move this initial state into a `gsap.from()` call within the IntersectionObserver/ScrollTrigger logic so the elements are in the DOM visibly by default.

Restructure the HTML inside the `mega-offer` dropdown to create a two-pane layout (e.g., a left column for high-level categories and a right area for the detailed links), matching the reference video.
Change the `.hero-connecting-line` SVG from a dashed line to a solid line, and implement a draw-down animation using `stroke-dasharray` and `stroke-dashoffset`.
